details: a `Decompressor` write held about 16 bytes of memory per byte it decoded, and a write returns everything the input it has completes, so a hostile gzip HTTP response of about 62 KB took an Xo HTTP client 1 GB, and up to about 16 GiB under the default `max_size` of 1 GiB; output is now copied once (a write inflating 1.3 MB to 206 MB peaked at 3.34 GB, now 420 MB). One DEFLATE block fed in small writes cost quadratic time (it was decoded again from its start on every write: a 4 MB block in 16 KB writes took 2706 ms, now 56 ms; a hostile 64 MB block about 11 minutes of CPU). Input after a zlib or raw stream's end is dropped instead of kept, and a `Decompressor`'s first error is returned by every later `write` and `finish` without decoding, as Go's readers keep theirs. Affected: 0.51.0 and earlier.
